clue.text: Watch Hodgson's old gypsy man collecting scrap

indicators.note: time collecting scrap means the first word gathers up the second, which follows on behind it

parts.note: Ralph Hodgson's poem 'Time, You Old Gypsy Man' addresses time itself by that name
a scrap is a small piece

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on a poet's elderly traveller as he picks up bits of scrap metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like an order to observe, but it is the noun, a clock you carry. Ralph Hodgson was an English poet; his best-known poem gives time that title.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a portable clock, an instrument for keeping time.

clue.text: Can batsman be so entitled to free food?

definitions.text: Can batsman be so entitled to free food?

parts.words: Can batsman be so entitled to free food?
parts.note: a cricket opener who got at the tinned food would be called this, and the kitchen tool frees food from its tin

explanation.surface: A cricketer wonders whether his title earns him meals on the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an opener is a batsman who goes in first; the joke names the gadget that opens cans.
explanation.definitionFit: The kitchen gadget cuts open a metal can to release its contents.

clue.text: Apt name for Thursday's child

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says Thursday's child has far to go, so a long distance would fit as a name; it is also a boy's name

explanation.surface: A fitting thing to call a baby born on a Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' says 'Thursday's child has far to go'; this boy's name is also a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles is a boy's name and also a long distance, fitting the child with far to travel.

clue.text: In a religious house it has preference

indicators.note: in a religious house means the word it is placed inside the building

parts.note: a priory is a monastery or convent run by a prior

explanation.surface: Within a monastery it is given precedence.
explanation.definitionFit: Priority means precedence, the right to be considered first.

clue.text: An African drunk — a gin: type

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An African tipsy on gin, of a certain type.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Egypt is an African by nationality.

clue.text: English flower festival

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A celebration of flowers grown in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast of the Resurrection.

clue.text: Shaw with bushy features

parts.note: shaw is an old word for a small wood or thicket, and the bushy features are its shrubs, though the surface points at George Bernard Shaw's famous beard

explanation.surface: The playwright George Bernard Shaw, with his bristling beard and eyebrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an archaic and dialect word for a thicket or little wood, which is full of bushes.

clue.text: Arrive with lady .half cut:- should be a laugh

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: half cut means the word lady loses its front half, keeping only the back part

explanation.surface: Turn up with a tipsy woman and you're in for some fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims LADY to its second half, DY.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedy is amusing entertainment, something that is good fun.

clue.text: Condition for a dream

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a vision is something seen in a dream

explanation.surface: The requirement to make a dream come true.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision is a clause or stipulation in an agreement.

clue.text: Constable's support, perhaps

parts.note: John Constable the English landscape painter would rest his canvas on a stand, not a police officer's backing

explanation.surface: The backing a police constable might get from colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is the English landscape painter John Constable, not a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters prop the canvas on a wooden stand while working.

clue.text: Fully in order to cancel

indicators.note: put in order means these letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Completely in line with the plan to call the whole thing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is fodder and 'order' alone is the signal: FULLY plus IN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify something is to make it void, to annul or cancel it.

clue.text: Call for a mount say before battle?

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: said aloud, a mount is 'amount', and an amount is a sum
Mons in Belgium was the first British battle of the First World War, 1914

explanation.surface: A rider asking for a horse to be brought out just before the fighting starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to hear 'a mount' as one word, amount, which is a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons is a formal call or order to appear, as before a court.

clue.text: Problem set for one in picture

definitions.meaning: someone who models or sits for a painting or photograph

explanation.surface: A puzzle set for whoever is in the photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a tricky question, and also a person who strikes attitudes for a portrait.

clue.text: Steps must be taken to make this punishment work

definitions.text: Steps must be taken to make this punishment work

parts.words: Steps must be taken to make this punishment work
parts.note: the 'steps' are literal footsteps on a turning wheel, the old prison penalty where inmates walked endlessly to drive machinery

explanation.surface: Action is needed if this penalty is going to be effective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps must be taken' sounds like measures to be adopted, but here it means real treading on a Victorian prison wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian prison wheel was turned by convicts climbing its steps, a punishment that powered mills.

clue.text: Glass of grog a feature of Pickwickian retirement

definitions.meaning: a last alcoholic drink taken before bed
Mr Pickwick in Dickens retires to bed in the tasselled cloth hat worn at night

explanation.surface: A tot of rum was part of how Mr Pickwick spent his old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests leaving work, but it means going to bed. Mr Pickwick, of Dickens's Pickwick Papers, is pictured in bedclothes and a sleeping cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a bedtime drink and the soft cap once worn in bed share this name.

clue.text: One to have a row with in City thoroughfare

definitions.text: One to have a row with in City thoroughfare

parts.words: One to have a row with in City thoroughfare
parts.note: a row is a trip by oar, and the thoroughfare is a canal of Venice

explanation.surface: Someone you might argue with in a busy city street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but it means rowing; the City is Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian boatman propels his craft with a single oar along the canals.

clue.text: Accuser not clear so dispute remains

indicators.note: accuser not clear means the word for clear is removed from the word for accuser

parts.note: a plaintiff brings a case against someone in court
plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: Since the prosecution's case is unconvincing, the argument goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' reads as 'continues', but points to what is left of PLAINTIFF once PLAIN goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor dispute.

clue.text: Smart and having influence, he knows the ropes

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp-witted, smart
weight means influence, as in carrying weight

explanation.surface: A clever and powerful man who understands how things work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knows the ropes' sounds like experience, but means a boxer in the ring, which is roped off.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer in the lightest weight division fights inside the roped ring.

clue.text: One boy's name is another's — we get mystified by the sound of it

definitions.text: mystified by the sound of it

parts.note: a means one
Tom is a boy's name
Ed is another boy's name

explanation.surface: One boy is called by another's name, and we are baffled by how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads 'a Tom is Ed'. 'Mystified' said aloud is 'mist-ified', turned into a fine spray, which 'by the sound of it' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomised liquid has been reduced to a fine spray, as if turned into mist.

clue.text: Let out for nutty receiver

definitions.meaning: a way of escape, a place to slip away to
the hole a bolt goes through before a nut is fastened on it

explanation.surface: Released to provide for a crazy radio set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' seems to mean mad, but refers to the nut on a bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt-hole is a refuge for escape, and literally the opening that takes a bolt.

clue.text: No duck for this princess

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing; 'ran one' (scored a single) means the batsman avoided it, and the Indian princess's title can be read that way

explanation.surface: This royal lady is not served duck at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is cricket's score of zero, so a batter who 'ran I' (one run) has avoided it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or princess, the wife of a rajah.

clue.text: At first try one out in case he can help

indicators.note: at first means these two letters are placed at the front
out means the letters of try and one are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Try someone out early on, in case they can be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like 'initially', but AT is placed first; 'out' reorders TRY ONE as TORNEY. The 'case' is a legal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer acts on a client's behalf in a legal case.

clue.text: Outline the beginning of the sailing ship

indicators.note: the beginning of sailing means only its first letter is taken

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: Describe how the sailing ship got started.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief outline.

clue.text: Undergo spelling test — this book is part of 'it

indicators.note: is part of means the book's name sits inside the opening words of the clue

explanation.surface: Take a spelling test; this book is included in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Undergo spelling'; 'test' and 'it' only complete the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four accounts of Christ's life in the New Testament is a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Place in hotel with space to hide

parts.note: to cloak something is to cover it up or conceal it
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A spot in a hotel where there is room to go into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels keep a room where guests leave coats and bags.

clue.text: Copper coin made to measure .

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A copper coin produced to a standard size.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length, about the length of a forearm.

clue.text: A list round about King Arthur's time

definitions.meaning: a set of figures or facts arranged in rows and columns
the knights of King Arthur met at the famous Round one

explanation.surface: A list of things dating from roughly the age of King Arthur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round about' seems to mean 'roughly', but it describes Arthur's round piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a tabulated list of data, and Arthur's knights sat at the Round Table.

clue.text: Probably a white-collar union candidate

parts.note: the union is marriage, and the white is the wedding dress, not office work

explanation.surface: Likely a recruit for an office workers' trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white-collar union' suggests a trade union of office staff; the union is a wedding and the white is her dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman being married usually wears white at the ceremony.

clue.text: Created New York, for example?

parts.note: made, constructed, in the past tense, and also describing a densely developed urban area like Manhattan

explanation.surface: Founding a great city such as New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up area is one covered with buildings, and the phrase can also be read as 'constructed upwards'.

clue.text: Hang about the House demonstrating

indicators.note: about means the word for hang goes around the abbreviation for house

parts.note: to swing is to hang and move freely, as from a rope
HO is the usual abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Loitering round Parliament while staging a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' suggests the Commons, but only gives the abbreviation HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing something is exhibiting or displaying it.

clue.text: Blazer carried by unhappy lover

definitions.meaning: something that blazes, a flaming light
the idiom of carrying one for someone means loving them without return

explanation.surface: A sports jacket worn by a heartbroken romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' suggests the jacket, but it is anything that blazes.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a burning brand, and to carry a torch for someone is to love them unrequitedly.

clue.text: Building we hear is intended for occupation

parts.note: a lodge is a small building, such as a gatehouse

indicators.note: we hear means what follows is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A building, so we're told, that is meant to be lived in.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgement is the act of taking up residence, or a position held by occupying forces.
